sentences.text: Iteravis is an extinct ornithuromorph bird found in the Early Cretaceous Jiufotang Formation of Liaoning Province, China.
The species name honors Dr. Fritz Huchzermeyer, an archosaur paleontologist who died just before the genus was described.
Unlike Archaeorhynchus, this bird consumed larger food particles, though the precise details of its diet remain unknown.
Scientists debate whether Iteravis is a synonym of Gansus zheni or a distinct genus closely related to Gansus within the family Gansuidae.
In 2021, Ju and colleagues concluded that Iteravis huchzermeyeri and Gansus zheni are the same species based on a detailed comparison.
Conversely, O'Connor and colleagues (2021) treated them as distinct species despite observing small differences of uncertain taxonomic significance.
Recent phylogenetic analyses by Wang et al. (2025) and Huang et al. (2026) recovered Iteravis as the sister taxon to Gansus yumenensis.
It lived during the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous, between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
